purpose: The fourth prospective episode, and an attack on this session's own headline number. Committed before any G6 code exists.
symptom: Six of the ten dimensions G5 reports as measured are 1.0 readings taken on omega-capability-probe-suite-1.0.0, the saturated instrument: reasoning, mathematics, unknownUnknown, longHorizon, robustness and resourceEfficiency. G3 changed the suite version to omega-outcome-measured-suite-1.0.0 and carried those values forward unchanged. The instrument comparison already refuses to subtract a score taken on one suite from a score taken on another, and then the generation record quietly does exactly that inside a single vector.
whyThisMattersMoreThanTheOtherFindings: G5's mean of 0.810125 is mostly ceiling carried over from the instrument that was replaced for being saturated. The separation reported at G3 is real for the four dimensions actually re-measured and is diluted by six that were not. Every claim this session made about the mean rising from G3 to G5 is a claim about stale numbers moving.
resolutionCriterion: Resolved only if the reported mean is computed from dimensions actually measured under the recording suite, and carried-forward readings are excluded from it rather than counted. Not resolved by relabelling, by adding a note, or by the mean happening to move.

prediction.claim: The honest mean over only the dimensions measured under the outcome suite will be materially lower than 0.810125.
prediction.estimate: The four genuinely measured dimensions are software 0.6667, crossDomain 0.3333, selfDiagnosis 0.5 and calibration 0.60125, so the honest mean should land near 0.53.
prediction.confidence: High on the arithmetic, which is checkable. What I do not know is whether recordGeneration can be made to refuse a carried-forward reading without invalidating the G0 through G5 records already written.

whatWouldFalsifyTheConcern: The six carried-forward dimensions turning out to have been re-measured under the outcome suite after all, which would make them current rather than stale.
